Actually, let me reconsider. When I click a charcoal spot to spawn the player, the green diamonds are replaced by charcoal spots. The player appears at the bottom-left. What if the goal is to have the player "collect" the charcoal spots by clicking on them?
But I tried clicking a charcoal spot and it had no impact. Unless... the player needs to be ADJACENT to the charcoal spot first?
Or maybe the goal is to click the green diamonds in a specific order, and the charcoal spots indicate the correct order. The G border might be a "highlight" showing which green diamond to click next.
Let me try a different sequence: click the green diamonds in the order indicated by the charcoal spots.
When I click (19, 18), charcoal appears at (19, 30). This is between (19, 24) and (19, 36).
When I click (19, 24), charcoal appears at (19, 12). This is to the left of (19, 18).
So the pattern seems to be: clicking a green diamond creates a charcoal spot at a position that's symmetric or related to the clicked diamond's position.
What if the goal is to click green diamonds such that the charcoal spots end up in positions that MATCH the green diamond positions? Like, click (19, 18) to get charcoal at (19, 30), then click (19, 36) to get charcoal at (19, 12)... and somehow this creates a pattern.
